conversation.content: The TestFlight build is out. Now I need my first 3 beta testers but I have no idea where to find them. Break this down for me?

goal.title: Launch the MVP of my budgeting app

success_criteria: Core flows work on a real phone
milestones.title: MVP works end to end
3 beta testers using the app weekly

expected_output.message_to_user: Here's "Recruit 3 beta testers" broken into four one-hour steps. The screener matters most: three well-matched testers who actually budget monthly will teach you more than twenty random downloads.

tasks.description: Draft a short invite (who it's for, what they get, time commitment of 15 minutes a week for 2 weeks) and three screening questions, e.g. how they track spending today.
tasks.expected_result: One invite text and a 3-question screener form link.
tasks.title: Write a 5-sentence beta invite and a 3-question screener

acceptance_criteria: Screener has 3 questions that separate real budgeters from curious visitors
methods.instructions: Paste the invite text and the screener link.

pass_criteria: Invite and screener meet the criteria
verification_protocol.rationale: Both are texts that can be reviewed directly.

tasks.why_it_matters: The screener filters for people who actually budget, so their feedback reflects your real users.

tasks.description: Pick three communities (forums, subreddits, local groups) where budgeting is discussed, read each one's self-promotion rules, and post the invite only where it is allowed.
tasks.expected_result: Three live posts with links and a note of each community's rules.
tasks.title: Post the invite in 3 communities where people discuss budgeting

acceptance_criteria: Each community's promotion rules are respected

verification_protocol.rationale: Public posts can be opened and checked.

tasks.why_it_matters: Going where your users already talk about the problem beats generic advertising at this stage.

tasks.description: Schedule a short call with each qualified applicant, watch them install the build and set up their first budget, and note where they hesitate.
tasks.expected_result: Call notes for 3 testers with at least 3 observations each.
tasks.title: Run a 20-minute onboarding call with each tester who passes the screener

methods.instructions: One question to check the notes reflect real calls.
questions: Which observation surprised you most, and what will you change first?

pass_criteria: 3 calls logged with at least 3 concrete observations each
verification_protocol.rationale: Structured, specific notes are hard to fabricate convincingly and are what the next step needs; calls themselves are not recorded, so confidence is medium.

tasks.why_it_matters: Watching first use reveals friction that testers rarely report in writing.

tasks.description: Create a short form for bugs and ideas, and a weekly message asking what they used the app for and what annoyed them.
tasks.expected_result: A form link and the check-in message text scheduled for 2 weeks.
tasks.title: Set up a feedback form and a weekly 2-question check-in message
tasks.why_it_matters: A fixed weekly rhythm keeps testers active for the two weeks the milestone requires.

contrastive.critique: "Research the market" and "Do marketing" are not actions anyone can start or finish, and "tell me what you did" is not a verification for work that leaves checkable artifacts.

tasks.description: Look into who might use your app.
tasks.title: Research the market
tasks.why_it_matters: You need to know your market.

tasks.title: Do marketing
tasks.why_it_matters: People need to hear about it.
